findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify in the plan where `parse_class_slots` is called with the actual config-file sub-table (e.g., `_read_llm_file_table(repo_root).get('model_classes')`) — either add this one-liner to `LLMConfig.from_env()` (storing slots on the config object) or explicitly assign the responsibility to cc33 with the exact sub-key to extract.
evidence: Plan scope: 'src/rebar/llm/config.py — only the env-var docstring block for the nine new vars … Any larger change here means the split above was not respected.'
parse_class_slots signature: `def parse_class_slots(table: Mapping[str, Any] | None)` — the table arg must come from somewhere
config.py `_read_llm_file_table()` returns the flat `[tool.rebar.llm]` dict; `[tool.rebar.llm.model_classes]` is a nested sub-table reachable via `.get('model_classes')`
cc33 plan says 'consume the fallback array that the schema ticket already parses' but does not specify it will extract the sub-table — it could trivially call `parse_class_slots(None)`
All unit tests in test_model_classes.py call `parse_class_slots({...})` directly; none test that config-file values flow through from `LLMConfig.from_env()`
findings.finding: The plan does not specify the call-site that extracts `[tool.rebar.llm.model_classes]` from the loaded config file table and passes it to `parse_class_slots`. `LLMConfig.from_env()` already reads the flat `[tool.rebar.llm]` dict via `_read_llm_file_table()`; extracting `.get('model_classes')` and passing it to `parse_class_slots` is a one-liner, but the plan's scope says `config.py` gets ONLY env-var docstring additions and is otherwise frozen. This means any consumer (including the sibling ticket cc33) that calls `parse_class_slots(None)` will silently ignore all config-file-sourced class settings — only the nine env vars will take effect.
findings.location: Approach section / Scope section ('config.py — only the env-var docstring block')
scenarios: An operator sets `[tool.rebar.llm.model_classes] frontier = {model='gpt-4o', provider='openai'}` in pyproject.toml; cc33's call to `parse_class_slots(None)` silently ignores it and uses the `claude-opus-4-8` default.

The cc33 implementer has no spec telling them to call `table.get('model_classes')` and so ships the path that ignores config-file values — all ACs in this ticket pass green while the feature is broken end-to-end for file-configured operators.
findings.suggested_fix: Either: (a) add `model_class_slots: dict[str, ClassSlot] = field(default_factory=dict)` to `LLMConfig` and in `from_env()` add `model_class_slots=parse_class_slots(table.get('model_classes'))` — this keeps the integration in one well-tested place and lets cc33 read `cfg.model_class_slots`; or (b) if cc33 owns the call, explicitly state in this ticket's scope that cc33 must call `parse_class_slots(_read_llm_file_table().get('model_classes'))` and add an acceptance criterion verifying a config-file-sourced class value is resolved correctly end-to-end.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a one-sentence note to the Approach section explaining that `pydantic-settings` (the idiomatic prior art for structured env-backed config) is ruled out by the existing stdlib-only constraint on `rebar.llm.config`, and that the hand-rolled dataclass approach deliberately mirrors that constraint.
evidence: config.py module docstring: 'stdlib-only — importing it never pulls the agent runtime (pydantic-ai) or anthropic — so import rebar.llm stays dependency-free'
pydantic-settings is a well-established solution for exactly this pattern (BaseSettings + env_nested_delimiter for per-field structured env overrides) — it is prior art the plan does not cite.
Plan does not mention the stdlib-only constraint as justification for the hand-rolled approach.
findings.finding: The plan never states why `pydantic-settings` (which natively handles structured nested env overrides via `env_nested_delimiter`, exactly this use case) was not used, leaving the anti-repackaging question open. The real reason — that `rebar.llm.config` is explicitly stdlib-only so importing `pydantic_settings` is barred — is present in the code but absent from the plan.
scenarios: A reviewer or future contributor asks 'why not use pydantic-settings?' and has no plan-level answer, potentially prompting a rework attempt that would break the stdlib-only invariant.

Reference this doc from AGENTS.md if that file governs contributor conventions.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Evaluate using `KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS` in `scripts/gen_env_registry.py` (the designed extension point for helper-based env reads) as an alternative to the `_ENV_VAR_NAMES`+`literal_reads` double-dict workaround; if the workaround is genuinely necessary (e.g. the helper signature doesn't fit), document in the plan why `KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS` was considered and rejected.
evidence: Plan states: 'spelled out one string per entry -- NOT built with an f-string -- because scripts/gen_env_registry.py … statically scans for a string-LITERAL argument to os.environ.get(…)'

scripts/gen_env_registry.py:37-47 defines KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS as the designated extension point: 'helper name -> (0-indexed position of the env-name argument, name prefix). Signatures verified against the current tree; extend by adding a row here.'
The plan does not mention KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS as an alternative or justify why it was bypassed in favour of the literal-reads pattern.
model_classes.py:106-116: the literal_reads dict calls os.environ.get() for all nine vars on every call to _env_override, even when only one field is needed — a consequence of the workaround design.
findings.finding: The plan introduces a novel two-dict static-scanner workaround (`_ENV_VAR_NAMES` + `literal_reads`) without considering the existing `KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS` extension mechanism in `scripts/gen_env_registry.py`, which is the prior-art, designed extension point for exactly this situation. Adding `_env_override` (or a thin named helper it calls) to `KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS` with its arg-position would cover all nine vars with two lines in the generator rather than 18 lines of boilerplate in the module, and without the side-effect of executing 9 `os.environ.get` calls on every invocation of `_env_override` regardless of which field is queried.
scenarios: A future author adds a tenth env var using the same pattern, duplicating the workaround instead of the designed extension mechanism, growing the boilerplate indefinitely.
The 9-call-per-invocation cost is paid even on config paths that only need one field (e.g. resolving a single class slot during startup).
If KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS is the right mechanism here, the scanner workaround in model_classes.py is unnecessary complexity that obscures the module's intent.
findings.suggested_fix: In `scripts/gen_env_registry.py` add one row to `KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS`: `"_env_override": (1, "")` (or whatever arg-position carries the env-name), then replace `_env_override`'s body with a single `os.environ.get(name)` call. This makes the scanner see the env vars through the helper path, eliminates the boilerplate dicts, and removes the 9-call-per-invocation overhead.
